newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS SAYS SEMICONDUCTORS PICKING UP.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS SAYS SEMICONDUCTORS PICKING UP.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday its semiconductor business was beginning to pick up, after first quarter operating profits at its components and semiconductors unit slipped year-on-year.

"Semiconductors is experiencing a far better income and sales level than we might have hoped. It's starting to turn up. Our own book-to-bill is strong...is above one. That's encouraging," Philips vice chairman Dudley Eustace told a results press conference.
But Eustace said price pressures continued to be rather strong, estimating them to be around nine percent.

"It's still tough out there, but we feel that in general the semiconductors business is starting to show some greater strength in this first quarter than initially perhaps we had envisaged," Eustace said.
"I'm not looking to a very long horizon, but generally speaking, business has picked up," he added.
Income from operations in the components and semiconductors division totalled 429 million guilders, down from 496 million guilders in the first quarter of 1996.
Sales were stagnant at 3.29 billion guilders, as higher sales of components were offset by lower semiconductor sales.
